gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-buhid: Uniform strokes, wide gaps, and hardly any capital swagger from Bushcraft. It earns its place when big and brief, while Noto Sans Buhid, a plain sans with open curves and a high x-height, handles the rest.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Wide-set, uniform, quietly artistic: that's Bushcraft. Bushcraft is happiest as a big, spaced-out display line, while Noto Sans Chakma, a sans with open, uncrowded mouths, does the steady reading.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-elbasa: Laser-cut precision defines Bushcraft, with one cutting width throughout and wide spacing, set against Noto Sans Elbasan's large, open-ended lowercase. Down the page, those open terminals keep lines from clogging up.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-ethiop: Expressive and wide-spaced, Bushcraft draws every curve at a constant thickness. Shrink Bushcraft and its display character fades, while Noto Sans Ethiopic, a sans-serif with a sturdy build and far-hanging c terminals, carries the text.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-glagol: Approachable body letters in Noto Sans Glagolitic stay readable small. And Bushcraft skims above them on a stroke weight that never changes, leaving a plain sans to do the quiet work.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-gujara: Noto Sans Gujarati reads clean and modern, its curved strokes stopping short of turning inward and leaving large open counters. Beside Bushcraft's closed, uniform curves, that sans feels breezier.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-gurmuk: Noto Sans Gurmukhi reads clean, its terminals flaring outward like tongs. Bushcraft brings closed letters in an unvarying rhythm, and that closed-versus-open tension is the pairing's real draw.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-hanuno: Bushcraft spaces its letters wide and keeps every stroke uniform. Beneath it, Noto Sans Hanunoo, a sans filling most of the line height with open terminals, supplies a grounded, readable counterweight.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-hebrew: Steady lines, no pressure variation, and wide spacing give Bushcraft an expressive look. And Noto Sans Hebrew, a sans-serif with a dominant midsection and wide curve gaps, keeps the text easy going.
gen-dafont-bushcraft-gf-noto-sans-inscri: Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian is a sans-serif with big open eyes. Bushcraft has no hairlines to thin its stems, while the body's deep middle band keeps text flowing smoothly line after line.
